notes: "Each word brings a flower or a diamond." / "Each word brings a snake or a toad." — 'brings' is a slightly abstract use for A1 and reads stiffly; the next scene clarifies it, but clearer would be: "When you speak, a flower or a diamond falls from your mouth." (and the same pattern for snakes and toads).
"One day, a poor woman came there." — 'came there' is a little unnatural; better: "One day, a poor woman came to the fountain."
"The mother ran at the younger girl." — 'ran at' (to attack) is a phrasal use an A1 reader may misread as 'ran to'; simpler: "The mother was very angry. She ran after the younger girl."
Only a few words lie outside beginner vocabulary ('fairy' is unglossed but standard in A1 fairy tales); comprehension holds overall.
"She carried a big pitcher to a far fountain and back." — 'a far fountain' is not natural modern English; better: "She carried a big pitcher to a fountain far from the house, and back again."
"Five or six pearls and as many diamonds fell from her mouth." — 'as many' is above A2; simpler: "Five or six pearls and five or six diamonds fell from her mouth."
"So I give you a present." — slightly odd; "So here is a present for you." stays within present simple and sounds natural.
"The mother ran at the younger daughter." — same 'ran at' point as A1; consider "The mother ran after the younger daughter angrily."

issues.quote: "Do you think I came here to give you water? Of course, I brought this silver flask just for you! Go and drink from the fountain yourself!" said the older girl.
issues.problem: The middle sentence is sarcastic, but at B1 nothing signals the sarcasm ('Of course,' reads as a sincere statement). A learner will read it literally — she brought the flask for the lady — which directly contradicts the next sentence and the point of the scene. B2/C1 mark the irony with 'I suppose', B1 does not.
issues.fix: "Do you think I came all this way to give you water? Do you think I brought this fine silver flask just for you? Go and drink from the fountain yourself!" said the older girl.

notes: "The mother scolded her for coming back so late" and the rest of the level respect the B1 grammar limits (no conditionals or passive).
Close and natural rendering of Perrault; sarcasm is clearly marked with 'I suppose'. Quiz keys are correct and unambiguous.

Genuinely literary and faithful (half league, 'Well, daughter?' / 'Well, Mother?', dowry reasoning). The added line about the mother not noticing she said 'my daughter' and the prince's growing astonishment are tasteful embellishments, not padding.
Softening the elder sister's death in the wood to 'went far away from home' is appropriate for a 4+ app and consistent across all levels.

summary: A faithful, age-appropriate retelling of Perrault's 'Diamonds and Toads' (Les Fées) at all five levels, with correct quiz keys and a suitably softened ending. B1 fails on one concrete point: the elder sister's sarcastic line 'Of course, I brought this silver flask just for you!' is unmarked and will be read literally, contradicting the scene. A1/A2 have minor wording notes ('ran at', 'a far fountain', 'as many diamonds') that are worth fixing but not blocking.
